groups.summary: Confirmed on real headless Chromium (Python 3.13.16, repo HEAD 064148f). The whole group comes from one problem: Element.get_position (element.py:519) is typed as returning `Position | None`, but it never returns None. (1) When DOM.getContentQuads returns [], which happens for display:none, for a button nested in a display:none parent, for a hidden file input and for a detached node, it runs `raise Exception('could not find position ...')` at line 529. The `except IndexError: return None` at the end can never fire, because quads[0] only runs when the list is non-empty. (2) When the element has no tree, the guard `not self.parent` at line 520 calls the parent property, which raises RuntimeError('could not get parent since the element has no tree set') at line 367. As a result, click() (line 418) fails inside its cosmetic `await self.flash(0.25)` at line 432 and never sends the JS `el.click()`. Calling apply('(el)=>el.click()') directly on the same element does work. The `if not position: warn; return` branches in mouse_click, mouse_move, mouse_drag and flash are dead code, and screenshot_b64 raises a plain Exception instead of the RuntimeError its docstring promises.

groups.refinements: For a detached node, getContentQuads in this Chromium returns [] rather than a 'Could not compute content quads' ProtocolException, so it takes the same raise-Exception path. groups.summary: I could not refute it. On real headless Chrome 141.0.7390.37 (Python 3.13.16, repo copy of zendriver imported), DOM.getContentQuads returns an empty list, not an error, for any element without a layout box. That covers display:none, descendants of a display:none parent, the hidden attribute, input type=hidden, content of a closed <details>, <option> inside a closed <select>, and detached nodes. Element.get_position (element.py, inside the try, `if not quads: raise Exception('could not find position ...')`) turns the empty list into a bare Exception. Its `except IndexError: return None` can never run: quads[0] is guarded, and Position() unpacking would raise ValueError, not IndexError. click() awaits the cosmetic flash(0.25) before the JS `el.click()`, so the exception escapes and the JS click is never sent. A JS click on the same element through apply() works. For elements with no tree (Tab.get_all_linked_sources, or element.create(node, tab) without a tree), click() first sets _remote_object. get_position's guard then reads self.parent, which raises RuntimeError('could not get parent since the element has no tree set'), so click() always fails on those elements. The `if not position/pos` fallbacks in mouse_click, mouse_move, mouse_drag, flash and screenshot_b64 never run for hidden elements. This is not deliberate. Upstream nodriver (its current element.py) wraps get_position in flash() with `try ... except (Exception,): return`, so click() works on hidden elements there. Upstream zendriver main has the same flash/get_position/click code as this branch, so the regression is zendriver's own. Local git history is squashed at 5c1a005, so I cannot see when the change was made. No test asserts the raising behaviour.

groups.summary: Two of the three sites are real. In Connection._register_handlers (connection.py ~L709), a bare `except:` wraps `await self.send(domain_mod.enable(), _is_update=True)`. When a wait_for timeout or task.cancel() hits a pending Domain.enable, the CancelledError is swallowed and the domain is removed. Connection.send (L654, `await self._register_handlers()`) then sends the enable again and waits for it with no timeout left. If the enable never answers (for example a busy renderer), send() hangs forever on Python 3.11 and 3.13. SEED-X2 is real but sits in Element.mouse_click (element.py ~L574-577, `try: await self.flash() except: pass`), not Element.click, which calls flash without a try. A cancel or timeout that lands during flash is lost: mouse_click returns None, wait_for raises no TimeoutError, and the calling coroutine keeps running. SEED-X3 is refuted: UpstreamProxy.open_tunnel's `except BaseException as e` closes the writer and re-raises CancelledError.

Network.enable is sent at t=0.0 and sent again at t=0.3, right when the timeout fires. Await chain: send:654 -> _register_handlers:707 -> send:662 (await tx). task.cancel() is ignored the same way. Same failures on Py3.11. Real headless Chromium: page stuck in while(true), handler for runtime.ConsoleAPICalled, wait_for(tab.send(target.get_target_info()), 2.0) is STILL RUNNING after 8s, stuck on Runtime.enable. With the prototype it raises TimeoutError at 2.00s.

Wrong location: the bare except is in Element.mouse_click (around flash), not Element.click, which awaits flash(0.25) with no try. With a duck-typed tab whose Runtime.callFunctionOn (the flash call) never answers, task.cancel() during flash is lost: flow() runs past mouse_click and the task is not cancelled. wait_for(el.mouse_click(), 0.3) returns None, not TimeoutError, on Py3.11 and 3.13. Real Chromium (page whose styleSheets getter runs 4s of sync work after the click): repo returns None after 1.00s with no TimeoutError; prototype raises TimeoutError at 1.00s. Severity is a lost cancellation rather than a hang, because flash is the last statement.

open_tunnel's `except BaseException as e` only converts OSError/IncompleteReadError/TimeoutError and re-raises everything else. test_open_tunnel_propagates_cancellation (silent proxy, cancel during CONNECT) passes on the unmodified repo: the task ends cancelled. Unrelated cosmetic issue: on Py>=3.11 asyncio.TimeoutError is builtins.TimeoutError, a subclass of OSError, so a proxy timeout is reported as 'proxy closed the connection: TimeoutError()' and not 'timed out waiting for the proxy'. Seen on 3.11 and 3.13.

fix_assessment.diff_summary: connection.py, Connection._register_handlers: replace the bare `except:` around `await self.send(domain_mod.enable(), _is_update=True)` with two handlers. First, `except asyncio.CancelledError:`, which removes domain_mod from self.enabled_domains if present and re-raises; the enable may never have reached the browser, and a later call re-sends it, which CDP treats as idempotent. Second, `except Exception:` with the existing log and remove logic unchanged; the noqa is dropped because E722 no longer applies. element.py, Element.mouse_click: `except:  # noqa` -> `except Exception:` around `await self.flash()`. proxy.py unchanged. Full patch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/Q12-fixsafety/q12-fix.patch. ruff check and ruff format --check both pass.
fix_assessment.risks: No locks added, so no lock-ordering issues. _register_handlers runs outside _open_lock, and inside _attach_session a CancelledError now leaves through `async with self._attach_lock`, which releases the lock cleanly. Behaviour changes callers will notice: CancelledError, KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit and GeneratorExit now propagate out of send()/aopen() and mouse_click() instead of being swallowed. Remaining minor issue (not fixed, low probability): if the cancel lands in Connection.send's own `_register_handlers()` call, which runs after `self.mapper.update({tx.id: tx})`, the never-sent outer Transaction stays in mapper until aclose. aclose then calls set_exception on it, giving a 'Transaction exception was never retrieved' log. This needs aopen's _register_handlers to have failed with an Exception, or a handler added concurrently during _prepare_headless/_prepare_expert. A fuller fix would pop tx on BaseException around that call, or create tx after _register_handlers. Also, when the cancellation leaves mid-loop, the trailing cleanup of unused enabled_domains is skipped; the next _register_handlers recomputes it, so this is harmless. mypy on the prototype: 332 errors, identical to an untouched copy (all pre-existing, in cdp/), so no new errors.

fix_assessment.risks: No locks, tasks or cancellation are involved, so there is no re-entrancy, deadlock or lock-ordering risk. Error paths: ProtocolExceptions from resolveNode or getContentQuads (stale ids after navigation) still propagate as before. Behaviour changes callers would notice: (1) click() on a display:none, detached or removed element now sends the JS el.click() and returns instead of raising. (5) get_position() returns None instead of raising, which matches its existing Optional annotation. groups.summary: I tried to refute this group and could not. Its central claim holds. Config.__repr__ (repr, str, print, f-strings, logging that actually emits), Config.__call__ and a read of the Config.user_data_dir property all run mkdtemp on the template Config and leave _custom_data_dir False. After that, every deepcopy in Browser.__init__ carries the same temp path. I verified the next steps with real headless Chromium 141. The second zd.start(config) fails after 2.5 s with 'Failed to connect to browser', and its stop() runs shutil.rmtree on the profile directory the first browser is still using. The failed-start leaks are also real. A bad browser_executable_path leaks one empty uc_* directory per attempt, and so does a connect-existing start with nothing listening. Two parts of the claim are wrong or overstated. First, Browser.__init__'s eager '%s' % vars(self) debug line materialises only the browser's own deepcopy, never the template, so it causes the leaks but not the shared profile. Second, Chrome does not hand the launch over to the first browser's process: it aborts. The deleted profile also has almost no visible effect on the first browser.

Aborting now to avoid profile corruption'. The variant 'without a failure, the first stop() deletes the other's profile' cannot happen with two launched browsers running at the same time, because the second launch always aborts on b1's live SingletonLock (verified). Reusing the template one browser at a time works fine.

groups.summary: All five config-argument claims reproduce on Python 3.13.16 against the repo copy, with my own probes. The worst one is K5. Config.add_argument rejects any argument whose lowercased text contains headless, lang, data-dir, data_dir, no-sandbox or no_sandbox. Browser.start passes --load-extension through add_argument, so Browser.create raises ValueError, and the browser never starts, whenever an extension path contains one of those substrings (for example .../headless-scraper/ext or /opt/LanguageTool). K2: argv carries duplicate copies of flags that Config adds itself (confirmed in /proc/<pid>/cmdline of a real Chromium). When the values differ, Config's copy comes last and silently overrides the user's browser_args value, because Chrome uses the last value of a repeated switch. K4: Config stores the caller's non-empty list by reference, so add_argument mutates it and leaks into other Configs built from the same list. K1: the browser_args property returns sorted(defaults + user args). It does not merge --disable-features and does not dedupe, so it differs from Config(). K3: each start() appends another --load-extension to browser.config. On an ordinary restart the duplicates never reach a launched Chromium, because start() keeps the host/port it set and takes the connect_existing path; they reach the real argv only if host/port are cleared by hand.

member_verdicts.note: With Config(browser_args=['--disable-features=Foo','--no-first-run','--mute-audio','--mute-audio']), the property shows two separate --disable-features entries and two copies each of --no-first-run and --mute-audio. Config() returns one merged --disable-features and only one --no-first-run. The property also leaves out --user-data-dir, --no-sandbox and the webrtc flags. Within the library, only Config.__repr__ reads it, so the impact is cosmetic: it only misleads someone inspecting the config. Related: the property has no setter, so `config.browser_args = [...]`, which docs/quickstart.md shows, raises AttributeError (docs are out of scope).

Without a browser, Config() returned 2 copies each of --headless=new, --no-sandbox, --lang=de-DE, --disable-webgl, --disable-webgl2, both webrtc flags and --user-agent=UA. In real Chromium, /proc/<pid>/cmdline held 2x --headless=new and 2x --no-sandbox, plus conflicting pairs ['--lang=fr-FR','--lang=de-DE'] and ['--webrtc-ip-handling-policy=default_public_interface_only','--webrtc-ip-handling-policy=disable_non_proxied_udp']. To check what Chrome does with a repeated switch, I passed browser_args=['--user-agent=FromBrowserArgs/1.0'] with user_agent='FromConfigAttr/1.0'; Browser.getVersion reported 'FromConfigAttr/1.0', so the last copy wins. Identical duplicates are therefore harmless. The real effect is that Config's appended flags (including the default disable_webrtc=True) silently override what the user set in browser_args. __call__ only dedupes user args against the defaults and --user-data-dir, not against the user list itself or the flags appended later.

Real Chromium, Config with add_extension(ext/plain). The 1st start has one --load-extension. After stop() and start() on the same instance, browser.config._browser_args and browser.config() hold 2 copies, but that 2nd start raised ConnectionRefusedError: host/port are still set on the config, so it takes the connect_existing path and launches no process. After clearing host and port by hand, a 3rd start launched Chromium with 3 identical --load-extension entries in its real argv. Browser.__init__ deepcopies the config, so a fresh Browser.create(cfg) that reuses the caller's Config sees only 1 copy. Since Chrome uses the last value and the copies are identical, the effect is cosmetic.

mine=['--window-size=800,600']; c=Config(browser_args=mine): c._browser_args is mine is True. After c.add_argument('--mute-audio'), mine == ['--window-size=800,600','--mute-audio'], and a second Config(browser_args=mine) also emits --mute-audio. An empty list is not aliased, because `if not browser_args` swaps in a fresh []. This only bites when the user calls Config directly: zendriver.start and Browser.create deepcopy the Config, so the add_argument inside Browser.start never touches the caller's list.

add_argument raised ValueError for --disable-features=LanguageDetectionAPI, --accept-lang=fr-FR, --enable-features=TranslateUI,LanguageSettings, --load-extension=/home/me/headless-scraper/ext, --load-extension=/opt/LanguageTool and --disk-cache-dir=/tmp/user-data-dir-cache, and accepted --mute-audio. The error message says to use a Config attribute, but none exists for these. End to end: Config.add_extension('<scratch>/ext/headless-scraper/ext') followed by Browser.create(cfg) raised ValueError from Browser.start's internal add_argument('--load-extension=...'). No browser was launched, so a legitimate extension cannot be used from such a path. Passing the same flags through the browser_args constructor argument skips validation entirely, which is inconsistent.

groups.refinements: K3: the duplicates never reach a launched Chromium on an ordinary restart. After stop(), start() reuses the host/port it assigned and takes the connect_existing path, which fails with ConnectionRefusedError (that is a separate restart issue). The start() branch for a process that has exited (create(config=self.config)) also keeps host/port, so it takes the same path. K2: identical duplicates are harmless because Chrome uses the last value. The defect worth fixing is precedence: Config-appended flags (user_agent, lang, the default disable_webrtc=True policy, headless) override conflicting values the user put in browser_args. Also, browser_args=['--headless=new'] with headless=False leaves config.headless False, so the headless UA patch in start() is skipped. K5 is the member with real user impact: Browser.start aborts with ValueError for any extension directory whose path contains a blocked substring, and the substring list also blocks unrelated flags such as --accept-lang and *Language* feature names. A fix should match flag names exactly (split on '=' and compare the switch name) and should not route the internal --load-extension through the user-facing validation. K1: the only internal consumer is __repr__. K4: aliasing only shows when Config is used directly, since Browser deepcopies.

groups.summary: Confirmed on repo code (Python 3.13.16, real Chromium 141 plus browser-free tests). Config.__repr__ (config.py, Config.__repr__ ~l.254-255) calls getattr() on every property in the class dict. That includes user_data_dir, whose lazy getter (Config.user_data_dir ~l.140-151) runs mkdtemp, stores the path on the template and leaves _custom_data_dir False. Browser.__init__ (browser.py ~l.259) deep-copies the template, so every browser gets the same 'temporary' profile. With real Chromium the second zd.start(config) fails with 'Failed to connect to browser', and its stop() rmtree's the profile that b1 is still using. Browser.__init__'s eager `logger.debug('...%s' % vars(self))` (~l.274) runs repr on the browser's own copy, so a temp dir is created at construction even with debug logging off. start() raises FileNotFoundError at the executable check (~l.539) before anything cleans it up, so one uc_* leaks per failed call. For connect-existing, start() always calls self.config() (~l.565), which creates the dir. When the connection fails, stop() hits the early return in Browser._stop (~l.875, `if not self.connection and not self._process: return`) and skips _cleanup_temporary_profile, so that dir leaks too. The minimal local fix has two parts: (1) __repr__ reads self._user_data_dir for user_data_dir and no longer calls the getter; (2) the early-return path of _stop calls _cleanup_temporary_profile. Optionally, (3) the debug log in __init__ becomes lazy. This fixes the repr-driven sharing and both leaks. Calling config() or reading config.user_data_dir on a template still makes browsers share a profile; fixing that needs a design decision.

groups.refinements:
1) Which change fixes which member: the __repr__ change alone fixes A3.6/A9.3/B16.5 (print/repr/logging trigger), A3.7 and B16.6(a). The lazy debug log is then only belt-and-braces. B16.6(b) needs the _stop early-return cleanup.
2) Residual that the minimal fix does not cover: config() (which the docstring offers as a way to inspect the args) and reading config.user_data_dir on a template still materialise one shared, non-custom temp dir. On the prototype both give 'shared profile: True'. Smallest fix, prototyped in .../R14-fixsafety/pkg2: right after the deepcopy in Browser.__init__, add `if not self.config.uses_custom_data_dir: self.config._user_data_dir = None`. It passes 8/8 of my tests and the same 29 repo tests. It changes behaviour, though: a temp dir already created on the template is orphaned (an empty uc_ leak), and a user who pre-seeded the auto temp dir would silently get a fresh one. So it is a maintainer decision, not part of the minimal patch.
3) The browser.py line ~259 deepcopy in the group 'where' is only the propagation point. The root cause is the side-effecting getter being reached through __repr__.
4) Optional polish: _cleanup_temporary_profile reads the lazy getter, so on the new early-return path a never-started browser creates and then deletes a uc_ dir (net zero, verified). Guarding on self.config._user_data_dir would avoid that.

fix_assessment.diff_summary: config.py Config.__repr__: `if k == "user_data_dir": v = self._user_data_dir` (with a short comment), then `elif isinstance(v, property): v = getattr(self, k)`, so repr never runs mkdtemp (an unset dir prints 'user_data_dir = None'). browser.py Browser.__init__: `logger.debug("Session object initialized: %s", vars(self))` (lazy; checked that it still renders the dict when DEBUG is on). browser.py Browser._stop: the early-return branch `if not self.connection and not self._process:` now runs `await self._cleanup_temporary_profile()` before `return`.
fix_assessment.risks:
No locks are involved, so there is no re-entrancy or lock-ordering concern. _cleanup_temporary_profile only awaits asyncio.sleep in its retry loop, so a cancel just stops the cleanup. Exceptions are contained: a mkdtemp or rmtree OSError inside the getter is caught by the existing try/except, so stop() of a never-started browser cannot raise (worst case about 0.75s of retries).

Behaviour changes callers could notice: (a) repr(config) shows 'user_data_dir = None' instead of a freshly created path when no dir was set. (b) stop() of a never-started or failed connect-existing browser now deletes its non-custom temp dir. That dir is normally its own; it is only someone else's in the residual config()/read-sharing case, where a never-started copy's stop() could now delete a live sibling's profile (contrived: Browser(config) + stop() without start()). The pkg2 variant removes that hazard.

Not fixed: config()/reading user_data_dir on a template still shares one profile, which needs the design-level reset in Browser.__init__ (see refinements).

groups.summary: Four of the five config-argument claims are real in the code, but under a refute/realism lens most of them are cosmetic. K5 is the one that matters. add_argument rejects any argument whose lowercased text contains 'lang', 'headless', 'data-dir', 'data_dir', 'no-sandbox' or 'no_sandbox'. Browser.start passes '--load-extension=<paths>' through add_argument, so an extension whose path contains one of those substrings makes Browser.create raise ValueError before Chrome is launched. Examples: a 'languagetool' folder, a 'headless-scraper' project, or a Windows user called Lang/Lange, whose %TEMP% also holds unpacked .crx files. K1 (the browser_args property differs from __call__) and K2 (user args that repeat Config-owned flags are not removed) are confirmed, but Chrome tolerates the duplicates (verified): identical boolean switches are harmless and for value switches the last one, Config's, wins. K4 (Config keeps a reference to the caller's list) is confirmed only when the caller uses Config directly and calls add_argument. Browser.__init__ deep-copies the config, so zendriver.start/Browser.create never mutate the caller's list. K3 is refuted: a duplicated --load-extension never reaches Chrome, and would be harmless if it did.

member_verdicts.note: Config.browser_args (property, config.py ~L136) returns sorted(_default_browser_args + _browser_args). With browser_args=['--disable-features=Foo'] the property shows two --disable-features entries while __call__ shows one merged entry. The property also lacks --user-data-dir, --no-sandbox and the webrtc flags, and keeps a user arg that duplicates a default. Nothing in zendriver reads it except Config.__repr__ (used by the debug log in Browser.__init__). The __init__ docstring names config() as the list passed to the browser. The property has no setter (assignment raises AttributeError). Impact is limited to display/debug output: cosmetic, low realism.

In Config.__call__ (~L194-227) user args are filtered only against the defaults plus --user-data-dir (and the filter is computed before extend, so duplicates within the user's own list survive too). Config's own --headless=new, --no-sandbox, --lang, --user-agent, --remote-debugging-port, --disable-webgl and webrtc flags are appended afterwards with no check. Verified duplicates: --headless=new x2, --no-sandbox x2, --disable-webgl x2, --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy x2. Real Chromium 141 headless launched fine with --headless=new x2 and --no-sandbox x2 (verified). For duplicated value switches the last one wins (verified with --window-size and --user-agent), and Config's copy comes last, so the outcome matches Config's settings. --lang has no effect on Linux, headless or headful under Xvfb (verified). Cosmetic. Hitting the duplicate itself is common (browser_args=['--no-sandbox'] while running as root in Docker), but it does no harm.

The add_argument call in Browser.start (~L558) does mutate self.config every start, but that config is the Browser's private deepcopy (Browser.__init__ ~L258). The caller's Config is never mutated (verified), and a second Browser built from the same Config gets one --load-extension (verified). The two restart paths never launch Chrome. (1) start() after stop() leaves config.host/port and self.info set from the first run, so connect_existing=True. No process is launched and connecting to the old port fails with ConnectionRefusedError (verified). (2) start() after the process died calls create(config=self.config), which also sees host/port set, launches nothing and raises 'Failed to connect' (verified). The doubled entry exists only in internal _browser_args. Even when passed, an identical --load-extension twice loads the extension once (verified).

Config.__init__ (~L92) stores the caller's list itself: c._browser_args is mine. c.add_argument() therefore appends to the caller's list, and a second Config built from the same list sees the added args. With a shared BASE list, c1.add_argument('--window-size=800,600') then c2.add_argument('--window-size=1000,700') makes c1's Chrome start at 1000x700 (verified, last switch wins), which is a wrong result. Not reachable through zendriver's own entry points: zendriver.start(browser_args=mine) and Browser.create(cfg) with an extension leave the caller's list untouched (verified, thanks to the deepcopy). An empty list is replaced by a fresh []. Low realism: needs direct Config use plus add_argument plus a reused list.

Config.add_argument (~L229-245) uses 'any(x in arg.lower() for x in [...])'. Verified rejected: --disable-features=LanguageDetectionAPI, --accept-lang=fr-FR, --enable-features=HeadlessModeX, --disk-cache-dir=/x/data_dir, and --load-extension= paths containing golang, C:\Users\Lang, headless-scraper. End to end with real Chromium: add_extension(.../ext/languagetool) or (.../headless-bot/ublock) makes Browser.create raise ValueError '"--load-extension=..." not allowed', and Chrome is never launched. The same extension loads fine when passed through constructor browser_args (verified), which is the only workaround. The blocklist dates from the initial import; the repo test asserts only that --lang=de-DE is rejected, not the substring breadth. Medium realism for extension users.

groups.refinements:
- K5 is the actionable member. The realistic trigger is not a user calling add_argument with odd flags but Browser.start's own --load-extension call. Case-insensitive matching means Windows profiles like C:\Users\Lang or Lange also block .crx extensions, which are unpacked under %TEMP%. A fix should match flag names exactly (e.g. the part before '='), not substrings, and should not route --load-extension through the user-facing validation.
- K1 and K2 are cosmetic: Chrome tolerates the duplicates and Config's value comes last and wins. Deduping is a cleanup, not a behaviour fix.
- K4 needs direct Config use, add_argument and a list reused across Configs or mutated later.
- K3 should be dropped as stated. The real defect it brushes against belongs to another group: a Browser cannot be restarted after stop() or after its process dies. config.host/port (and self.info) persist from the first run, so start() takes the connect_existing path and fails with ConnectionRefusedError or 'Failed to connect' instead of relaunching.
- Side observation, out of group: Browser.__init__ eagerly formats logger.debug('... %s' % vars(self)). That calls Config.__repr__, which reads the user_data_dir property and creates a temp profile dir. When start() then fails before launch (e.g. the K5 ValueError), the dir is never cleaned up: two empty /tmp/uc_* dirs leaked in my K5 run.

groups.summary: All five seeded leads reproduce on the repo code. Config.__call__ (config.py) never removes duplicate args, apart from user args that repeat the defaults. Config.browser_args returns sorted(defaults + user args) with nothing merged or removed. Config.__init__ keeps the caller's list (self._browser_args = browser_args). Config.add_argument rejects any arg that contains a blocked substring anywhere. Browser.start (browser.py) builds --load-extension through config.add_argument on every start. K5 is worse than the seed says: because Browser.start sends the extension path through add_argument, any extension whose absolute path contains 'lang', 'headless', 'data-dir' or 'no-sandbox' (case-insensitive, for example /home/lange/..., C:\Users\Langley\..., or a folder named language-helper) makes zd.start() raise ValueError before Chrome is launched. I showed this with real headless Chromium. K1 to K4 are cosmetic or minor wrong-result issues: Chrome uses the last value of a repeated switch, so identical repeats change nothing at runtime.

member_verdicts.note: Config(browser_args=['--disable-features=Foo','--mute-audio','--mute-audio']).browser_args returns two --disable-features entries and two --mute-audio, while config() merges the disable-features into one. Nothing inside zendriver reads this property, so only callers who inspect it or reuse it are affected (cosmetic). It can never equal config() exactly, and making it call self() would be a mistake: the user_data_dir getter lazily creates a temp profile dir, and __repr__ calls property getters. The safe fix is to apply the same merge and duplicate removal. Separate issue, out of scope: docs/quickstart.md shows `config.browser_args = [...]`, but the property has no setter, so that line raises AttributeError.

Browser-free: headless=True, sandbox=False, lang='de-DE', disable_webgl=True plus the same flags in browser_args gives --headless=new, --no-sandbox, --lang=de-DE, --disable-webgl and --force-webrtc-ip-handling-policy twice each. Real Chromium on the repo code: /proc/<pid>/cmdline contained --headless=new and --no-sandbox twice. The only duplicate removal is in Config.__call__, `arg not in args`, which compares user args against the defaults, user-data-dir and expert args only. Repeats among user args (for example --mute-audio twice) are kept too. No runtime effect, since Chrome uses the last value: cosmetic.

With util._start_process patched to capture params, two start() calls on the same Browser (host and port reset between them) gave 1 and then 2 --load-extension args. The cause is that Browser.start mutates self.config._browser_args through add_argument. The natural restart paths still hold host and port from the first start, so connect_existing=True and no new process is launched: stop()+start(), and start() after the process exited, which goes through create(config=self.config). The duplicate only reaches Chrome if the caller resets host and port, and the two copies are identical. Cosmetic, low realism. This same add_argument call is how K5 crashes start().

base=['--mute-audio']; Config(browser_args=base).add_argument('--window-size=800,600') leaves base == ['--mute-audio','--window-size=800,600']. This only happens with a non-empty list, because an empty one is replaced by a new []. Browser.__init__ deep-copies the config, so the --load-extension added by Browser.start does not leak into the caller's list. Only the caller's own add_argument calls do. Minor wrong-result, for example when a base args list is shared between several Configs.

fix_assessment.diff_summary: config.py: (1) __init__: self._browser_args = list(browser_args), a copy (K4). (2) New module helper remove_duplicate_args(args) that walks args in reverse and keeps the last copy of each identical arg. __call__ now returns merge_disable_features_args(remove_duplicate_args(args)) (K2). (3) In __call__, when _extensions is set, append '--load-extension=' + ','.join(str(_) for _ in self._extensions) before --enable-unsafe-extension-debugging (K3). (4) browser_args property returns sorted(merge_disable_features_args(remove_duplicate_args(defaults + user args))) (K1). (5) add_argument checks the switch name only: name = arg.split('=', 1)[0].lstrip('-/').lower().replace('_', '-'), and rejects if name is one of ('headless', 'user-data-dir', 'no-sandbox', 'lang') (K5). browser.py: Browser.start drops its getattr(self.config, '_extensions')/add_argument('--load-extension=...') block (K3, and the K5 start crash). About 30 lines changed; ruff format and check are clean.
fix_assessment.risks: All code involved is synchronous, so locks, re-entrancy and cancellation do not apply. add_argument no longer raises from start(). Behaviour changes callers could notice: (a) the caller's list is no longer aliased, so code that appended to its own list after building Config and expected the change to show up stops working (this only ever worked for non-empty lists). (b) After start(), browser.config.browser_args / _browser_args no longer contain --load-extension; it now appears only in config() output. (c) Exact-duplicate removal also applies to positional args, so a URL listed twice in browser_args now opens once; restrict removal to args starting with '-' if that matters. (d) add_argument accepts more args than before: every name the new check rejects contained one of the old blocked substrings, so nothing new is rejected. Args the old check rejected that are now accepted: anything that merely contains a blocked word, plus non-switch names such as '--data-dir'. '/'-prefixed Windows switches like /headless are still rejected. The existing test_add_argument_still_rejects_lang still passes. (e) The browser_args property output changes (merged and duplicate-free) but still differs from config() by design. mypy: 332 errors on both the untouched copy and the prototype, all in cdp/, none in core/, so no new errors.

groups.summary: I could not refute any of the four members; each one reproduces. Only B14.5 is a hang. Connection.wait() awaits the old listener's idle Event (Connection.wait, `await self.listener.idle.wait()`, connection.py:579) with no timeout and no check that the listener is still running. If the session's Listener is cancelled while idle is clear, that Event is never set, so `await tab`, tab.wait() and Tab.get(url) on the same tab (tab.py:513) hang forever. This happens when the tab is closed, on browser.stop() from another task, or when Chrome is killed. The three seeds are real but minor and unlikely to be hit. SEED-C1: after ConnectionClosed every later send fails fast with ConnectionClosedError and never reconnects; nothing hangs. SEED-C2: the race is only reachable by calling Connection.aclose() directly while a connect is in progress. SEED-C3: the leak is small and temporary, about 1.3 KB per entry, and Chrome's late reply clears it, for example on navigation.

member_verdicts.note: Fake peer closes with 1011: listener stops, conn.websocket stays set, conn.closed reports False, three sends raise ConnectionClosedError right away, and the server sees only 1 connection. After a deliberate aclose(), the next send does reconnect (2 connections). Real Chromium with MAX_SIZE patched to 200000 and a 300 KB evaluate result (client sends 1009): Chrome stays alive and accepts a fresh Connection, but browser.connection and tab.evaluate fail with ConnectionClosedError for good. Setting websocket=None by hand restores both. Not a hang, and Browser.stop() still works. It only matters when Chrome outlives the socket: a message over 256 MiB, the 900 s ping timeout, or a dropped network link to a remote browser. Realism: low.

With a 0.3 s delayed connect, aclose() called during the connect returns at once (websocket is None), the in-flight send then succeeds, and the socket and listener stay open until a second aclose(). Realism is very low. Browser._stop skips connection.aclose() when closed is True (websocket is None while connecting), and for a local browser the process kill closes the late socket. A tab's aclose() racing _attach_session is cleaned up by the later browser-connection aclose, which detaches every session. Reaching it needs a user calling the documented internal aclose() at the same moment, and the result looks like the existing design where a send after aclose reconnects.

Fake peer that never answers Runtime.evaluate: 5 sends timed out by wait_for leave 5 cancelled Transactions in the mapper, and aclose() clears them. Real Chromium: 200 timed-out never-settling evaluates leave 200 entries, about 1282 bytes each (tracemalloc). Chrome answers all of them on navigate or reload, and the mapper drops to 0 (verified). No functional effect: the listener and _fail_pending_transactions skip transactions that are already done. Small, bounded leak; realism low.

Real headless Chromium 141, Python 3.13. Control (busy page that goes idle after 1 s): wait() returns after 1.11 s. Busy page (console.log every 40 ms, Runtime enabled) closed by Target.closeTarget, tab.close(), browser.stop() from another task, or killing the Chrome process: the waiter is still pending after more than 8 s, with its stack stuck at Connection.wait connection.py:579 and listener.running=False. A 0 ms close raises ProtocolException, and a close at 100 ms or later returns normally. An immediate click-to-window.close() raised 0/6 times and never hung. Realism: medium.

groups.refinements:
B14.5:
- It hangs only if the tab's session listener is busy (idle clear) when the session detaches.
- On a quiet page with no domains enabled, the window is only about the listener's time_before_considered_idle (0.1 s; 0.75 s in interactive mode) after the last session message. wait()'s own Target.getTargetInfo reply counts as such a message, so the window measured 20-80 ms after the call.
- A close that lands before the getTargetInfo reply makes wait() raise ProtocolException instead of hanging. That is the case for an immediate click-to-window.close().
- On pages with a steady stream of events (handlers or manually enabled Network/Runtime/Page domains), the window covers the whole wait.
- Affected: wait() with t=None, `await tab`, Tab.get(url) on the same tab (tab.py:513), and get/set_local_storage when target.url is empty.
- Not affected: wait(t) with a number (it uses wait_for), and Browser.get.
- Triggers: Target.closeTarget, tab.close() from another task, page window.close(), browser.stop() from another task, and a Chrome crash or kill.
- Nothing else ends the wait: websockets keepalive does not touch the Event, and a new Listener created later has a new Event.
- Not specific to a Python version (the Event is simply never set).

SEED-C1:
- Severity is wrong-result/cosmetic, not hang. The connection is permanently dead and `closed` reports False, but later sends raise at once.
- It matters only when Chrome survives the socket close.

SEED-C2:
- Only reachable through a direct Connection.aclose() during the first or re-opening aopen. Browser.stop does not trigger it (stop skips aclose when closed is True), and the process kill bounds it for local browsers.

SEED-C3:
- The entry lives only until Chrome replies, the session detaches or the connection closes. Chrome replies to pending awaitPromise evaluates on navigation or reload.
- Only commands that are never answered accumulate, at about 1.3 KB each.

groups.summary: Both members reproduce on real headless Chromium (chromium 141) on Python 3.13.16 and 3.11.17. Connection._prepare_expert and Connection._prepare_headless (zendriver/core/connection.py) check their done flag, await one or two _send_oneshot calls, and only then set the flag. Nothing serialises this and nothing checks whether the session is still the same one. (1) When two first sends run at the same time (asyncio.gather, or Tab.set_local_storage with 2 items), Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument is registered twice. After the next load, element.attachShadow() throws 'RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded'. (2) A detach (tab.aclose()) while the first send is inside the prepare step leaves _prep_headless_done=True, or _prep_expert_done=True, on the detached connection. The next send reattaches a new session but skips the override: navigator.userAgent and the HTTP User-Agent header contain 'HeadlessChrome', or the expert attachShadow override is missing. fix_assessment.diff_summary:
zendriver/core/connection.py only (full diff in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/R16-fixsafety/prototype.diff):
(B14.5) Listener.run: add `self.task.add_done_callback(lambda _: self.idle.set())`. A stopped listener counts as idle, so every exit path wakes wait(): break on cancel, ConnectionClosed, an exception, or a cancel before the first step. A finally inside listener_loop would miss the cancel-before-start case.
(SEED-C1) Listener.listener_loop, ConnectionClosed branch: also set `self.connection.websocket = None` and clear enabled_domains and manually_enabled_domains, mirroring aclose(). After that, `closed` is True and the next aopen() reconnects and re-registers handlers.
(SEED-C2) Connection.aclose: wrap the session branch in `async with self._attach_lock:` and the websocket branch in `async with self._open_lock:` (with `if self.websocket is None: return` inside). An in-progress attach or connect then finishes first and is closed or detached by this call, instead of opening after it.
(SEED-C3) Connection.send: add `finally: self.mapper.pop(tx.id, None)` to the existing try around `return await tx`.
fix_assessment.risks:
Locks. asyncio.Lock is not reentrant, but aclose() is never called while the same task holds _open_lock or _attach_lock: aopen's except path only calls listener.cancel(), and __aexit__ and Browser._stop hold no locks. Lock order in tab.aclose is tab._attach_lock then browser._open_lock (via browser_connection.send -> aopen). That is the same order _attach_session uses, and the browser's aclose takes only its own _open_lock and calls the synchronous _detach_session(). So there is no inversion. A stress probe (5 concurrent senders plus 10 aclose cycles, delayed handshake) finished without a deadlock, with mapper empty and 0 server connections left.

Cancel paths. If aclose is cancelled while waiting for the lock, nothing changes and the lock is released (verified). The prototype raises more 'connection was closed' ProtocolExceptions in that stress run (50 vs 25), because connects that complete during a close are now closed too.

Behaviour changes callers would notice:
(a) aclose() can now block until an in-flight websockets.connect finishes (open_timeout defaults to 10s). tab.aclose() can now block until an in-flight Target.attachToTarget round trip finishes.
(b) After a peer close, the next send tries to reconnect to the same URL. If Chrome is dead, callers get OSError/ConnectionRefusedError from websockets.connect instead of websockets ConnectionClosed. Browser._stop now skips browser.close and aclose because closed is True, which removes a spurious warning. A reconnect does not restore Target.setDiscoverTargets autodiscovery; that is a pre-existing limitation.
(c) wait() / `await tab` now returns None when the listener stops, instead of hanging. A caller whose tab was closed carries on and gets an error on its next command. Raising ProtocolException('target session was detached') would be the alternative design.
(d) A dead Listener's repr now shows [idle].

A theoretical stale-listener clobber of a new websocket in the C1 branch cannot happen with C2's lock in place, because a reconnect cannot start before aclose finishes and a cancelled listener gets CancelledError. Not covered by these fixes: _send_oneshot's identical cancel leak, and the pre-existing 3.10/3.11 ValueError listener-death race on detach (cosmetic, reproduces on repo code).

fix_assessment.diff_summary: zendriver/core/connection.py (diff at .../R18-fixsafety/fix.diff): (a) Connection.__init__ adds self._prepare_lock = asyncio.Lock(), like _attach_lock and _open_lock. (b) In send(), the _prepare_expert()/_prepare_headless() calls run inside `async with self._prepare_lock:`, followed by `if self.websocket is None: raise ProtocolException("target session was detached")` before the Listener and Transaction are created. (c) _prepare_headless and _prepare_expert capture session_id = self.session_id first and only set the done flag when `self.websocket is not None and self.session_id == session_id`. (d) The expert script is wrapped in `if (!Element.prototype._attachShadow) { ... }` so a duplicate registration is a no-op.
fix_assessment.risks:
Re-entrancy: the lock covers only the _prepare_* calls. Those call only _send_oneshot, then _send_transaction, then websocket.send, and never call send() or aopen(), so the lock is never acquired twice. It is released before _register_handlers' nested send(). The nested send from aopen->_register_handlers takes the lock before the outer send reaches it, one after the other, not nested.
Lock ordering: tab._attach_lock is held while browser_connection._prepare_lock is taken (through browser_connection.send in _attach_session). Nothing is acquired while tab._prepare_lock is held, so there is no cycle.
Cancel and error paths: `async with` releases the lock. A detach fails the pending oneshot, which _send_oneshot swallows, so the lock is freed promptly. The prepare oneshots have no timeout, so concurrent sends now wait for the first send's prepare. In the repo each of them already awaited its own identical oneshot, so liveness is unchanged.
Caller-visible change: a send whose session was detached during prepare now raises ProtocolException('target session was detached') earlier, with the same message as the existing later check. Previously, a tab with event handlers could silently reattach in _register_handlers' nested send and succeed on an unprepared session, which could also resurrect a session that a concurrent tab.aclose() had just detached. Now it raises, and the next send reattaches and prepares properly.
Remaining small window: if another task reattaches during the prepare, the first send's command may reach the new session before that session's prepare (the waiting task runs it right after). The flag is not left stale.
Not covered: the ValueError path from refinement 3. On a page that defines its own Element.prototype._attachShadow, the JS guard would skip the override (edge case).

Listener.listener_loop (connection.py, the `else: asyncio.create_task(asyncio.to_thread(callback, *args))` branch, ~L1002) runs every non-coroutine-function handler in a worker thread. Connection.feed_cdp (~L556) calls `asyncio.ensure_future(self.send(...))`, which needs an event loop in the current thread, so it raises `RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread 'asyncio_0'` there. Fetch.continueRequest is never sent and the paused request stays paused. I reproduced this on real headless Chromium 141 and against a browser-free fake CDP peer (Python 3.13). The asyncio failure is identical on 3.11 and 3.12. It is a regression: in the zendriver 0.10.1 wheel, sync handlers ran inline on the loop thread, so feed_cdp from a sync handler or lambda worked. The 0.10.2 change ('Refactor to asynchronous handlers to avoid blocking the listening loop') moved them to to_thread and broke it. The lambda/coroutine sub-claim is also real, but the plain 'lambda returning a coroutine' and 'object with async __call__' forms never worked, even in 0.10.1. Only 'lambda: asyncio.create_task(...)' (and any other loop-bound call from a sync handler) is new breakage from the same root cause.

zendriver/core/connection.py only (full diff in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/verify/R19-fixsafety/fix.diff).
(1) Connection.feed_cdp: the on-loop path is unchanged. Only when asyncio.get_running_loop() raises (the case that currently always fails) does it take the loop from self.listener.task.get_loop() and call loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.ensure_future, self.send(cdp_obj)). With no listener it falls through to the old ensure_future, which raises the same error as before.
```
loop = None
try:
    asyncio.get_running_loop()
except RuntimeError:
    # synchronous event handlers run in a worker thread (see
    # Listener.listener_loop), which has no event loop of its own
    if self.listener and self.listener.task:
        loop = self.listener.task.get_loop()
if loop is not None:
    loop.call_soon_threadsafe(asyncio.ensure_future, self.send(cdp_obj))
else:
    asyncio.ensure_future(self.send(cdp_obj))
```
(2) New module-level helper `async def _call_sync_handler(handler, *args)`. It runs `result = await asyncio.to_thread(handler, *args)` and then awaits the result if inspect.isawaitable(result). listener_loop's sync branch now does asyncio.create_task(_call_sync_handler(callback, *args)) in place of create_task(asyncio.to_thread(...)). Sync handlers still run off-loop.
ruff format and ruff check pass.
fix_assessment.risks:
Re-entrancy and locks: the worker thread only builds the send() coroutine object and schedules it. It does not wait for the result and holds no lock. send() runs on the loop thread and takes _open_lock/_attach_lock there as usual, so there is no new lock ordering and no deadlock. Reading listener.task concurrently is a benign race: any listener of the connection belongs to the same loop.

Errors: call_soon_threadsafe(ensure_future, ...) creates the task on the loop. A failing send therefore still shows up as 'Task exception was never retrieved', the same as the on-loop path (covered by test_feed_cdp_error_is_logged_like_on_loop_path). run_coroutine_threadsafe would have hidden the error in an unread concurrent future. If the loop is already closed, call_soon_threadsafe raises RuntimeError in the handler thread, which matches today's error class.

Behaviour changes callers would notice: (a) feed_cdp from sync handlers now works. (b) An awaitable returned by a sync handler is now awaited on the loop. This covers a lambda calling an async function and an object with an async __call__. A handler that returns a never-completing awaitable leaves one pending task. That task does not block the listener, the same as a hanging async handler. Handlers returning non-awaitables are unaffected.

Not fixed by design: loop APIs such as create_task or Event.set called directly inside a sync handler still fail or are unsafe in the worker thread. Fixing that means running sync handlers on the loop, an API/behaviour change that would undo the 0.10.2 non-blocking intent. Recommend a docstring note in add_handler and feed_cdp instead.

groups.refinements:
Exact trigger: an HTTP-scheme env proxy (http_proxy or HTTP_PROXY) is set. ALL_PROXY is ignored by urllib (assumed from source, not run). https_proxy alone does not trigger the HTTPApi part.

no_proxy has to be missing the literal '127.0.0.1' (or '*' or '.0.0.1'). The common 'no_proxy=localhost' does NOT protect, and neither do curl/Go-style CIDR entries such as '127.0.0.0/8'; Python ignores both (verified on 3.11 to 3.13). That widens the reach beyond 'no_proxy unset'.

It fails only when the proxy cannot serve the client's loopback, which covers a remote corporate proxy or one that denies loopback destinations (assumed). A same-host forwarding helper such as cntlm or px works for the HTTP leg (verified with a faithful fake forwarder). Even then, websockets>=15 fails on the CONNECT for the ws leg unless that helper allows CONNECT to arbitrary loopback ports.

The result is a fast failure (about 1.4s) with a misleading 'running as root / sandbox' message. A blackholing proxy instead stalls start() for about 10s per attempt, about 110s with defaults.

MacOS: urllib reads system proxy settings when no env vars are set. The default macOS bypass list ('*.local, 169.254/16') does not match 127.0.0.1 in _proxy_bypass_macosx_sysconf (logic verified on Linux; real macOS behaviour assumed). Windows registry proxies: assumed.

Fix scope: (a) bypass only loopback hosts (127.0.0.0/8, ::1, localhost) rather than dropping proxies for every host. connect_existing to a remote DevTools host might legitimately need the proxy. (b) Without a matching proxy=None for loopback in Connection.aopen's websockets.connect (connection.py about line 440), start() still fails for every user on websockets>=15, which is the default pip resolution because pyproject only pins >=14.0. On that path start() also leaks the Chrome process, which is a separate cleanup bug.

Workaround for users: add 127.0.0.1 to no_proxy.

groups.refinements:
1. The trigger is narrower than 'behind a proxy'. urllib uses only http_proxy/HTTP_PROXY for the http:// DevTools URL; https_proxy and all_proxy are ignored (urllib registers all_open but never calls it for http). HTTP_PROXY is also ignored when REQUEST_METHOD is set. So on websockets 14.x, an environment with only https_proxy is not affected.
2. On websockets>=15, the CDP websocket picks the first of ws, socks, https, http from the environment via websockets.uri.get_proxy. A very common setup with only https_proxy therefore breaks start() through Connection.aopen, even with the HTTPApi fix. websockets 15.0.1 is what a fresh `pip install zendriver` picks; uv.lock pins 14.1, so CI does not see it. A full fix also needs proxy=None there.
3. Test-isolation gotcha for whoever lands the test: urlopen builds its global opener once, on its first call in the process, and keeps the environment's proxies from that moment. A regression test in the real suite would silently pass on unfixed code if an earlier test had already called urlopen. My test sets monkeypatch.setattr(urllib.request, '_opener', None) to prevent that. The fix itself does not depend on this.
4. Separate bug, not R21: when start() fails at the websocket stage (seen with websockets 15 and a proxy), Browser.start raises without stopping the browser. The Chromium process tree and its /tmp/uc_* profile leak; I had to kill the process group I started. This probably belongs to whichever group owns start-failure cleanup.
5. Chromium also sends its own traffic (clients2.google.com time check) through the env proxy. That is the browser's own traffic and out of scope.

fix_assessment.diff_summary:
pkg, browser.py HTTPApi.__init__: add `self._opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))` with a 2-line comment. In HTTPApi._request, replace `urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10)` with `self._opener.open(request, timeout=10)`.

pkg2, additionally connection.py at module level after PING_TIMEOUT: `_NO_PROXY: dict[str, Any] = ({"proxy": None} if "proxy" in inspect.signature(websockets.asyncio.client.connect).parameters else {})`, and `**_NO_PROXY` in the websockets.connect(...) call in Connection.aopen. This is feature detection: {} on 14.1 and {'proxy': None} on 15.0.1, both checked. Passing proxy=None unconditionally raises on 14.1: 'TypeError: BaseEventLoop.create_connection() got an unexpected keyword argument proxy'. Alternative: bump pyproject to websockets>=15 and pass proxy=None directly.
fix_assessment.risks:
No locks, re-entrancy or cancel-path changes. HTTPApi holds no lock. The opener is per instance and OpenerDirector.open is already used from executor threads by the global urlopen. Error behaviour is unchanged: build_opener keeps HTTPErrorProcessor/HTTPDefaultErrorHandler, so HTTPError and URLError are raised exactly as before and test_connection still catches them.

Behaviour changes callers could notice:
(a) Code that relied on urllib.request.install_opener(...) to affect zendriver's DevTools requests is no longer honoured. Negligible.
(b) A user who reaches a remote browser (Browser host != loopback) only through an HTTP proxy loses proxied discovery. On websockets 14.x the CDP socket never used a proxy, so that setup could not work end to end anyway. With pkg2 on websockets>=15, it would also stop proxying the ws. If that matters, apply the bypass only for loopback hosts, or keep honouring an explicit no-bypass option. I consider unconditional direct connection the right default for a DevTools endpoint.

1) A1.5 and B14.7 depend on the Python version. Both reproduce on 3.12 and 3.13 but not on 3.11, where asyncio.wait_for wraps each recv in a task, so the session listener and _attach_session get to run between frames. A1.6 does not depend on the version.
2) On real Chrome the trigger is ordinary: the event loop is busy for about 200 ms (sync CPU work, time.sleep, a blocking handler) while the target is going away, so Chrome's frames pile up and are read in one burst. With an idle loop, Chrome's frames came in separate reads and zendriver behaved correctly in all trials.
3) The B14.7 hang has two causes that work together. (a) The detach is dropped because the session is not registered yet. (b) Error replies without a sessionId for a command sent on a session go to the browser listener. There, 'message["id"] in self.connection.mapper' misses, so the reply is silently dropped, even though _next_message_id says ids are shared so such replies could be matched. Fixing (b), by looking the id up in the session mappers, would turn this hang and similar ones into a clear 'Session with given id not found' error. The dead sessions also stay in browser.connection._sessions.
4) In the headless config the first stuck await is in _prepare_headless (_send_oneshot), not the user's command.
5) Separate from this group: after a detach, Connection.send can create a new Listener for an already detached connection (send checks the listener again after _prepare_headless, whose _send_oneshot swallows ProtocolException). That listener then dies with 'Task exception was never retrieved ... ValueError(no websocket connection)' from _receive_message. I saw this in the block=0 real-Chrome runs and the 3.11 runs.
6) A1.6: the leak lasts as long as the browser websocket (my assumption, not tested). The next send attaches a new session and works.

groups.summary: I could not refute any of the three members. Each one reproduced against real headless Chromium 141 through zendriver's public API. A1.5 and B14.7 need Python 3.12 or later: they reproduced on 3.12.3 and 3.13.16 and never on 3.11.17. A1.6 does not depend on the Python version. Both 3.12-only races need a structural condition. On 3.12+, asyncio.wait_for runs the coroutine inline, and websockets 14.1 Assembler.get returns buffered frames without suspending. So when the reply and the Target.detachedFromTarget frame are read in the same chunk, the browser Listener handles both in one task step. In A1.5 that step discards the reply already queued in session._inbox. In B14.7 it drops the detach, because the session is not yet in _sessions. For page targets Chrome sends the two frames 4-6 ms apart, so they only coalesce when the event loop is busy. For OOPIF removal the gap can be as small as 10 us, so they can coalesce even on an idle loop. A1.6 is a real orphaned Chrome session, but it is bounded: Chrome detaches it when the target closes or the browser websocket closes. 'Never detached' overstates it.

member_verdicts.note: Reproduced on real Chromium. The test command was tab.send(cdp.page.close()) on the tab's own session, with a sibling task doing 10 ms CPU chunks. The wire log shows 'reply-ok,detach' for the session, yet the caller got ProtocolException('target session was detached') in 8/8 and 20/20 runs (p7b, p7). Rates by load: 2 ms chunks gave 1/20, an idle loop 0/20, and 10 ms chunks on Py 3.11 0/20. A command in flight on an attached OOPIF while its iframe was removed failed 1/60 on an idle loop on 3.13, after Chrome had replied value 42 (p5), and 0/60 on 3.11. Mechanism (Connection._detach_session called from _receive_message): it sets _inbox=None, cancels the session Listener and fails the pending tx. Practical harm is mostly limited to commands that end their own session, such as Page.close or detachFromTarget on the same session. For unrelated in-flight commands the target is going away, and the same exception is the legitimate result in most races (52/60). Tab.close() already avoids this by sending close_target through the browser session (commit e81b66c).

Reproduced on real Chromium with Py 3.13 and 3.11 (p6). The tab came from browser.get(new_tab=True), so it was not attached. I cancelled the first evaluate while Target.attachToTarget was in browser_connection.mapper. Afterwards tab.session_id was None, and the next send attached a second session. tab.aclose() detached only that second one. The orphan session still answered a raw Runtime.evaluate with result 42 and its sessionId. Chrome detached it only when tab.close() closed the target, so the leak lasts as long as the target or the websocket, not forever. The window is the attach round trip of the first send on an unattached tab. First sends took 3-9 ms in total, including _prepare_headless. Internal timeouts (Tab.get and wait_for_ready_state, 10 s) practically never land in that window, so this needs a user-level short timeout or cancellation. I saw no functional zendriver impact. Low realism and low impact.

Reproduced on real Chromium with Py 3.13 (p4/p4b). I sent the first command to an unattached OOPIF Tab right as the parent removed the iframe. It hung in 2/30, 4/60 and 1/120 trials, and 0/60 on Py 3.11. Wire evidence: the attach reply was frame 195 and detachedFromTarget for the same session was frame 197. Both were handled before _attach_session registered the session. Chrome then answered the stuck command with {'id':80,'error':{'code':-32001,'message':'Session with given id not found.'}}, which has no sessionId. The browser listener dropped it because that id is not in the browser mapper. A second send on the same tab also hung. Only browser.stop() released the two stuck tasks, with ProtocolException('target session was detached'). The websocket keepalive does not help because the connection stays healthy. Through the public API: tab.select('#nope', include_frames=True, timeout=1) on a page that replaces a cross-site iframe every 120 ms, with a CPU-busy sibling task (10 ms chunks), stayed stuck for more than 15 s in 3/20 calls (p8c). The stack showed Tab.select, then _query_selector_all_with_frames, waiting on Network.setUserAgentOverride from _prepare_headless. On an idle loop it hung in 0/90 select calls (p8b).

Code (read fresh): Connection._attach_session (~L460) registers browser_connection._sessions[session_id] only after awaiting the attach reply. _receive_message (~L826) ignores detachedFromTarget for an unregistered sessionId, and routes a reply without sessionId only to the browser mapper. Listener.listener_loop (~L922) handles a reply only if its id is in self.connection.mapper. _detach_session (~L481) drops _inbox and fails pending transactions. Git history: everything comes from e81b66c (#280), where the Tab.close comment shows the reply-versus-detach race was known for close_target only. No test asserts the racy behaviour; tests/core/test_frames.py only checks session_id is None after close.
groups.refinements: 1) A1.5 and B14.7 require Python 3.12 or later. On 3.11, wait_for wraps the read in a task, so the session listener or the _attach_session continuation runs before the next read. They also require the reply and the detach to be parsed from the same socket read. That happens readily for OOPIF teardown, where the gap is 1 ms or less. For page targets the gap is about 4-6 ms, so the event loop must be blocked for at least that long when the reply arrives. 2) B14.7 only hangs if the target dies within about 1 ms after Chrome processed the attach. A slightly later destruction makes the attach fail cleanly with 'No target with given id found'. The hang ends only when the browser websocket closes, through browser.stop() or a connection drop. It defeats select/find(include_frames=True) timeouts, because those check elapsed time between iterations rather than wrapping each send. In headless mode the stuck send is the Network.setUserAgentOverride from _prepare_headless. 3) A1.5 matters mainly for commands that end their own session, such as Page.close or Target.detachFromTarget sent on the same session. For other in-flight commands on a dying target, the exception is usually what the caller would have got anyway. 4) A1.6 is low impact. Only one orphan leaks per attach attempt that is cancelled during the attach round trip, and Chrome reaps it when the target closes or the websocket closes. 5) Side observation outside this group: probes repeatedly logged 'Task exception was never retrieved ... ValueError("no websocket connection")' from Listener tasks. Connection.send recreates a Listener after aopen and _prepare_headless even if the session has just been detached, and that Listener's _receive_message raises with websocket=None.

fix_assessment.risks: Not assessed (refute lens). Possible fixes: (a) in _receive_message, remember session ids that were detached but not registered, and have _attach_session raise for them; or register the session from a done-callback on the attach transaction; (b) deliver the detach through the session inbox, or drain it before failing pending transactions, so queued replies resolve first; (c) route a reply without sessionId whose id belongs to a session's mapper to that session (ids are already shared per websocket), which turns any remaining B14.7 case into an error instead of a hang; (d) on cancellation of the attach, add a done-callback that records the session id or detaches it.

groups.summary: Confirmed with real headless Chromium 141 on Python 3.13 (repo copy imported). Browser.start() saves the host/port it picks itself into self.config (start, around lines 530-535), and _stop() never resets them. So start() after stop() takes the connect-existing path. It launches no Chrome, test_connection fails against the dead port, the stale self.info skips the 'Failed to connect' check, and Connection.send raises ConnectionRefusedError after about 2.5 s. After Chrome dies on its own, start() takes the `self._process.poll() is not None` branch and calls self.create(config=self.config). That copies the dead host/port, launches nothing and raises 'Failed to connect to browser'. Even with host/port reset by hand, stale targets stay in self.targets, so browser.get() fails with 'No target with given id found', and the restarted instance is not registered with asyncio_atexit again. For a Browser connected through host/port, `stopped` is True while it is live, the atexit hook skips _stop(), and a second start() opens a second websocket without closing the first. The old socket and its Listener stay alive.

(a) Reproduced in p1: the error comes from Connection.send, not from the 'Failed to connect' message, because self.info is stale. (b) Reproduced in p2: the create(config=self.config) branch copies the dead host/port and raises 'Failed to connect to browser'. Also, even on success that branch returns a NEW instance, so a caller that ignores the return value of b.start() keeps the dead object.

After a second b.start(), the connection is replaced but the old one is still open and its listener is still running. psutil ESTABLISHED sockets to Chrome went from 1 to 2. _atexit_cleanup() then leaves both open. Explicitly closing both brings it to 0, which proves the leak is these two sockets.

p4: stopped=True while connection.closed=False and tabs=1. The conftest-style `browser is None or browser.stopped` check returns True for a live browser. p5: at real loop close (asyncio.run end) the asyncio_atexit hook did not call _stop (spy recorded []) and connection.closed stays False. Caveat: _stop() sends Browser.close, so an exit hook that ran it would close an external Chrome the user launched. The wrong-result here is the `stopped` value, and the fix should not just make the exit hook close external browsers.

groups.refinements: Root cause, read from the code: Browser.start (browser.py around lines 530-535) writes the auto-chosen host/port into self.config, and connect_existing is decided only from `config.host is not None and config.port is not None`. So the config cannot tell user-supplied values from auto-chosen ones. Browser._stop (around lines 874-917) clears _process/_process_pid but not config.host/port, self.info, self.targets or self.connection. Extra findings: (1) The dead-process branch `return await self.create(config=self.config)` returns a new Browser instead of restarting self, so `await b.start()` without using the result leaves b dead even once host/port are fixed. The fresh instance is also registered with atexit while the old one stays in registered_instances. (2) update_targets never prunes the stale targets from the first run, so after a manual host/port reset tabs[0]/main_tab are dead Tab objects. (3) For B16.13, changing `stopped` so the atexit hook runs _stop() for connect-existing browsers would send Browser.close to a Chrome the user launched, which is a behaviour change. A fix should base `stopped` on the connection, and close only the websocket/forwarders at exit, not the remote browser. (4) The start() guard `if self._process or self._process_pid` does not cover connect-existing, so start() is not idempotent there (A3.10). Fix candidates: reset auto-chosen host/port in _stop (or keep a private flag for user-provided values), clear info/targets/connection on stop, and guard start() on `self.connection and not self.connection.closed`.
